## Configuration patches

Builders configure future runners; an existing runner retains its configuration snapshot. Sync and async variants use the same rules.

| Field                                            | Omitted or `undefined` patch                                     | Defined patch                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Walking `shouldFollowEdge`, `shouldExpandVertex` | Retain the previous predicate                                    | Callback replaces it; `null` clears it. Initial `null` also means absent.                      |
| Walking `replaceLimits`                          | Retain previous limits                                           | Replace the entire limits record; include every bound to retain.                               |
| `visitors` and `emitEvents` / `visitorPhases`    | Retain unspecified fields                                        | Patch visitor phases and selector fields independently, under their existing validation rules. |
| DAG `traversableTree` / `traversableGraph`       | Inherited keys and own `undefined` keys retain the active source | An own defined same-family source replaces it; an opposite-family source rejects.              |

Every supported configure field accepts an explicit `undefined` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: missing and undefined fields retain prior values. This includes tree sources, concurrency, scheduling fields, each visitor phase, and each in-order field. `null` clears only explicitly nullable fields (walking predicates and `transformChildHints`). Walking constructors accept `limits`; configuration patches use `replaceLimits` to replace that record. A patch containing the former `limits` key rejects, including own `undefined`. Malformed defined fields reject atomically before registrations or configuration change; an existing runner keeps its snapshot. DAG construction requires exactly one own defined source and configure cannot change its source family. Source getters are captured once per request, without calling source callbacks.

Public builders, helpers, mutation binders, execution options and nested option bags reject unsupported own string or symbol keys with `TypeError`, including non-enumerable keys and keys whose value is undefined. Source protocol objects can carry caller state and inherited methods; opaque data and IDs are not option bags. Path query options also reject unsupported own keys: `requirePathTo` / `requirePathsTo` accept only optional boolean `noRoot` and `noSelf` controls. Omitted or undefined controls use the default behavior, and accessors are captured once per query.

### Options and defaults

Choose the **surface** before building an option bag. Constructors require a source; `configure(patch)` changes future runners within that source family; existing runners keep their snapshots. Prepared definitions own topology. `run(options)` and `iterateEvents(options)` select execution/delivery rather than constructing a source. Public option bags reject unknown own keys, including symbols and present undefined fields.

#### Tree and DAG builders

These fields apply at construction and in source-preserving patches. Async counterparts accept value-or-promise callbacks; their `concurrency` bounds physical callback invocations, not host agents.

| Field                          | Default / values                                  | Surface and constraints                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `traversableTree`              | Required tree source                              | DFS/BFS; alternatively DAG tree-source mode. DAG fixes the source family at construction.                                                                                                                |
| `traversableGraph`             | Required graph source                             | DAG graph mode; exactly one defined source.                                                                                                                                                              |
| `transformChildHints`          | `null`; `(hints) => hints` replacement array      | DFS/BFS/DAG. Receives a copied hint array; may filter, duplicate, invent or reorder hints. Async transformers may return a promise. Null clears; undefined patches retain. Eager DAG topology is frozen. |
| `visitors`                     | Empty registrations for each family phase         | DFS PRE/IN/POST_ORDER, BFS LEVEL_ORDER, DAG ON_WORK_READY/ON_SUBGRAPH_READY. Each supplied phase patches independently.                                                                                  |
| `retainOriginalTreeStructure`  | `false`; boolean                                  | DFS/BFS only. Retains progressively discovered original topology and shallow payload identity.                                                                                                           |
| `retainOriginalGraphStructure` | `false`; boolean                                  | DAG only, including tree-source mode.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `concurrency`                  | `Infinity`; positive integer or `Infinity`        | Async tree/DAG only; synchronous builders and walkers reject it.                                                                                                                                         |
| `inOrder`                      | Field-wise defaults below                         | DFS only.                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `workCompletion`               | `'afterWorkReadyChain'` or `'externalSettlement'` | DAG. Empty/filtered normal chains also complete W under the default.                                                                                                                                     |
| `discovery`                    | `'lazy'` or `'eager'`                             | Graph-source DAG for eager; tree-source DAG accepts lazy/default. A fresh tree-source runner can still use prepare() for a preview.                                                                      |
| `syntheticRoot`                | `false`; boolean                                  | True requires a graph-source DAG; tree-source mode accepts false/default only. Hides an entry holder; MaterializedDagInput already supplies true.                                                        |
| `rootWorkDependencies`         | `'honor'` or `'ignore'`                           | DAG graph source only. Ignore suppresses root W gates, never C. Explicit use rejects for tree sources.                                                                                                   |
| `dependsOnWorkDefault`         | `'none'` or `'discoveryParentWork'`               | DAG graph source only. Applies only when the source omits its work declaration; explicit `[]` wins.                                                                                                      |
| `completedWork`                | No accepted seeds; `ReadonlySet<ID>`              | Fresh graph-source DAG runs. Copies membership, satisfies W only, rejects unknown IDs when discovery closes. See [completed-work rules](#discovery-and-completed-work).                                  |

DFS `inOrder` fields patch independently; arrays/ranges are copied:

| Field                       | Default                                  | Accepted input                                                                                            |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `afterChildIndices`         | `{ ranges: [{ from: 0, through: -2 }] }` | `{ indices: readonly number[] }` or `{ ranges: readonly { from, through }[] }`; safe integer coordinates. |
| `fallbackChildIndices`      | `{ indices: [-2] }`                      | Same selection union; negative positions address children from the end.                                   |
| `visitSingleChildParent`    | `true`                                   | Boolean.                                                                                                  |
| `visitAfterOmittedChildren` | `true`                                   | Boolean.                                                                                                  |

#### Hint transformation example

The transformer receives an owned copy of the input hint membership. It may filter, duplicate, replace or reorder hints within the source's hint type; it is not limited to sorting. These sync/async examples prune `drop` before discovery while keeping the input object unchanged.

<!-- standalone -->

```ts
import {
  DepthFirstTreeTraversal,
  AsyncDepthFirstTreeTraversal,
  DepthFirstPhase,
  ObjectTreeSource,
} from 'configurable-tree-traversal';

const input = { keep: 1, drop: 2 };
const source = new ObjectTreeSource(input);
const sync = new DepthFirstTreeTraversal({
  traversableTree: source,
  transformChildHints: (hints) => hints.filter((hint) => hint.key !== 'drop'),
}).createRunner();
const keys = [
  ...sync.iterateEvents({ emitEvents: [DepthFirstPhase.PRE_ORDER] }),
].map((event) => event.vertex.getData().key);
const asyncRunner = new AsyncDepthFirstTreeTraversal({
  traversableTree: source,
  transformChildHints: async (hints) =>
    hints.filter((hint) => hint.key !== 'drop'),
}).createRunner();
const asyncKeys: PropertyKey[] = [];
for await (const event of asyncRunner.iterateEvents({
  emitEvents: [DepthFirstPhase.PRE_ORDER],
})) {
  asyncKeys.push(event.vertex.getData().key);
}
if (
  keys.length !== 2 ||
  keys[1] !== 'keep' ||
  asyncKeys.length !== 2 ||
  asyncKeys[1] !== 'keep' ||
  input.drop !== 2
) {
  throw new Error('Expected the root and retained keep child');
}
```

#### Walking construction and patches

| Field                                    | Construction default / values                                         | Configure patch                                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `source`                                 | Required `GraphWalkSource` / `AsyncGraphWalkSource`                   | Replace the future runner's source; undefined retains.                                                        |
| `strategy`                               | `'breadthFirst'` or `'depthFirst'`                                    | Replace; undefined retains.                                                                                   |
| `revisit`                                | `'once'`, `'simplePaths'`, `'walks'`                                  | Replace, atomically validating the merged bounds.                                                             |
| `limits`                                 | No bounds for once; route modes require depth or candidate-read bound | **Not accepted** in a patch.                                                                                  |
| `replaceLimits`                          | **Not accepted** at construction                                      | Replace the entire limits record; include every bound to retain. Undefined retains the previous record.       |
| `shouldFollowEdge`, `shouldExpandVertex` | No predicate; callback or null                                        | Null clears; undefined retains. See [predicate contexts and bounds](#revisit-policies-predicates-and-bounds). |
| `visitors`                               | Empty phase-keyed vertex/edge/path registrations                      | Patch supplied phases.                                                                                        |
| `emitEvents`                             | `['vertex']`                                                          | Delivery selection; also available per execution call.                                                        |
| `visitorPhases`                          | `'all'`                                                               | Callback selection; also available per execution call.                                                        |

Every limit is a nonnegative safe integer: `maxDepth`, `maxAdmittedTargets`, `maxCandidateReadAttempts`. Zero is valid. Only maxDepth or maxCandidateReadAttempts satisfies the route-mode construction requirement. Bounds and topology are fixed for each created runner; use a new runner for larger bounds.

#### Preparation, prepared factories and sessions

| Surface                                                         | Accepted fields                                                                     | Defaults / ownership                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `prepareDag(input)`                                             | `traversableGraph`, `syntheticRoot`, `rootWorkDependencies`, `dependsOnWorkDefault` | Graph source required; false/honor/none policies. No visitors, seeds or completion policy.                     |
| `prepareDagAsync(input)`                                        | Same, plus `concurrency`                                                            | Async discovery; concurrency defaults to Infinity.                                                             |
| `dag.createRunner(options?)`                                    | `visitors`, `completedWork`, `workCompletion`, `retainOriginalGraphStructure`       | Empty visitors/seeds, afterWorkReadyChain, false. Topology/source/transform policies belong to the definition. |
| `dag.createAsyncRunner(options?)`                               | Same, plus `concurrency`                                                            | Returns a promise of a prepared runner; Infinity concurrency.                                                  |
| `dag.createWorkSession(options?)`                               | `completedWork`                                                                     | Independent progress; external settlement is owned by the session. No visitor option.                          |
| `dag.createAsyncWorkSession(options?)`                          | `completedWork`, `concurrency`                                                      | Returns a promise of a session; Infinity concurrency.                                                          |
| `bindDagWorkSession(runner)`, `bindAsyncDagWorkSession(runner)` | A runner configured for external settlement                                         | Binding is synchronous, shares runner progress, and creates local ticket authority.                            |

#### Per-execution selection

`run(options?)` and `iterateEvents(options?)` accept exactly these fields on concrete tree/DAG/walking runners. Sessions expose `advance()` rather than forwarding a per-call option bag.

| Field           | Initial default / values                                                  | Update rule                                                                                                                 |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `emitEvents`    | All tree phases; both committed DAG kinds; vertex-only walking            | A supplied readonly array replaces delivery selection; `[]` suppresses delivery. Undefined retains the effective selection. |
| `visitorPhases` | `'all'`, `{ include: readonly Phase[] }`, `{ exclude: readonly Phase[] }` | A supplied selector replaces callback selection; empty include disables, empty exclude enables all. Undefined retains.      |

Walking can establish these selectors at builder construction/configuration too. Tree/DAG builders use visitor registrations; their delivery/callback selectors belong to execution calls. Admitted chains retain callback snapshots; pending observations use current delivery selection. Explicit emission arrays narrow yielded records; absent/optional selectors retain the broad union.

#### Object source and rewrite options

`ObjectTreeSource(input, options?)` accepts the first three fields below. `rewriteObject(input, options?)` adds reconstruction/conversion and DFS configuration, **excluding** `traversableTree`; it owns the source. Bound `isComposite` and `getKeyPath` are observations, not option keys.

| Field                             | Default                                           | Meaning                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `getRootPropertyFromInputObject`  | Root mapper with the helper's default root key    | Adapt input to the root property. Required together with child mapper for narrow discovery types.                       |
| `getChildrenOfProperty`           | Own enumerable object/array properties            | Return input-domain hints; both mappers are mandatory with `fromProperties`.                                            |
| `resolveChildHook`                | Default resolution                                | Return useDefault/found/omitted for a child; graph metadata is forbidden.                                               |
| `rewrite`                         | Keep / default assembly                           | Post-order callback returning typed keep/delete/rewrite-patch operations.                                               |
| `convertRootValue`                | No conversion; output unknown                     | Required for a specific inferred/explicit output type unless using the assertion helper. Called only for present roots. |
| `assembleCompositesBeforeRewrite` | `false`                                           | Provide `assembledComposite` before invoking rewrite.                                                                   |
| `arrayIndexPolicy`                | `'compactInTraversalOrder'`                       | Alternative `'preserveNumericKeys'`.                                                                                    |
| `propertyCollision`               | `'error'`                                         | Alternatives `'firstWins'`, `'lastWins'`; custom assemblers own their placement/collisions.                             |
| `isArray`, `isObject`             | Array.isArray(value); non-null, non-array objects | Caller classification callbacks see current unknown-valued properties.                                                  |
| `assembleArray`, `assembleObject` | Built-in reconstruction                           | Caller assembly callbacks return unknown.                                                                               |
| `assembledMap`                    | New reference-keyed assembly map                  | Structural has/get/set cache accepting unknown writes.                                                                  |

Full callback declarations are linked from the [public symbol index](api-index.md). See [rewrite semantics](#rewrite-objects) for current/input/output domains, arrays, collisions and snapshot lifetime.

390	### Collection and forest sources
391	
392	All four DAG input helpers return a `MaterializedDagInput<Item, ID>` envelope with `{ traversableGraph, syntheticRoot: true }` options for DAG constructors and preparation. Pass or spread the whole envelope into DAG options; nesting it under `traversableGraph` is invalid and extracting only the source loses synthetic-root treatment. Walking materializers retain their names because they return actual `GraphWalkSource` protocols. Their data is the caller's item and their hints are IDs (`VertexTypes<Item, ID>`).
393	
394	Materialized lookup does not depend on live vertex data: the source accepts any rewrite-data context R, with an input specialization retained for ordinary Item/ID inference on TypeScript 4.7/4.9. The same envelope therefore composes with an explicitly disjoint R in sync/async DAG builders and helpers without assertions or new factory arguments. Discovery results and original views remain Item, and hint replacement remains constrained to input ID hints. This built-in capability does not relax live-context checks for user sources with narrow hooks. See the [executable disjoint-rewrite example](migration-idiomatic-api.md#dag-inputs-and-actual-sources).
395	
396	| Helper                                                  | Input and selectors                                                                                                                            | Membership and identity                                                                                                                                                                              |
397	| ------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
398	| `materializeDagInputFromRecords(items, selectors)`      | Iterable items; required `id(item)`; optional `children(item)`, `dependsOnWork(item)`, `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion(item)` return iterable IDs | Every item is catalogued, including disconnected entries. Any duplicate ID rejects, even the same record twice. Structural child IDs must exist in the catalog; `children` returns IDs, not records. |
399	| `materializeDagInputFromRoots(roots, selectors)`        | Iterable root items; same selectors, but `children(item)` returns iterable items                                                               | Expands iteratively. `children` returns records, not IDs. The same record can appear under multiple parents; different records with the same ID reject.                                              |
400	| `materializeDagInputFromRecordsAsync(items, selectors)` | Iterable/async-iterable items; value-or-promise selectors, with iterable/async-iterable edge results                                           | Awaits materialization, then returns an input envelope containing a synchronous discovery source.                                                                                                    |
401	| `materializeDagInputFromRootsAsync(roots, selectors)`   | Iterable/async-iterable roots; value-or-promise selectors; children yield records                                                              | Awaits materialization, then returns the same input envelope with shared-root rules.                                                                                                                 |
402	
403	Absent edge selectors mean empty lists. All four adapters reject the retired selector keys `dependencies` and `completionDependencies` with `TypeError`, even when inherited or present with `undefined`, before reading the input or invoking selectors. Use `dependsOnWork` and `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion` so a stale selector cannot silently drop dependency edges. Caller task-data properties may still use any names, including `dependencies`. Structural child edges and work/completion dependency edges remain distinct. Missing prerequisite IDs are left to the existing validator. Structural discovery cycles become `discoveryCycle` issues in `prepareDag`/`prepareDagAsync`; direct runners throw `DagDiscoveryCycleError`. The synthetic holder is hidden from public vertices, events, callbacks, and parent queries.
404	
405	Materialization copies collection membership and edge arrays once. Later edits to caller arrays do not change topology; item data and opaque IDs remain shared shallow values and are never frozen. SameValueZero IDs, including `undefined`, `null`, `NaN`, symbols, and objects, retain their identity. Selector errors and async rejections propagate unchanged. See the [quickstart](../README.md#quickstart-find-the-next-agent-tasks) for a complete flat catalog.
406	
407	Dependency vocabulary describes the same two milestone relations across layers:
408	
409	| Layer                                            | Wait for work (W)   | Wait for completion (C)           |
410	| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- | --------------------------------- |
411	| Collection selectors                             | `dependsOnWork`     | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`     |
412	| Sources and definitions                          | `dependsOnWork`     | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`     |
413	| Milestone queries                                | `milestone: 'work'` | `milestone: 'subgraphCompletion'` |
414	| Walking relation selections and definition diffs | `workDependencies`  | `subgraphCompletionDependencies`  |
415	
416	Structural `children` remain a separate relation. Walking those declarations observes links; it does not execute or satisfy milestones.
417	
418	### Reusable prepared DAGs
419	
420	`prepareDag(input)` returns `PrepareDagResult<Data, ID>`; `prepareDagAsync(input)` returns a promise of the same union:
421	
422	- `{ kind: 'valid', dag: PreparedDag<Data, ID> }` contains a reusable validated definition.
423	- `{ kind: 'invalid', issues: readonly DagDefinitionIssue<ID>[] }` represents validation failure and provides no executable definition. Source dependency failures contain one `{ kind: 'milestone', diagnostics: DagTraversalStallDiagnostics<ID> }` issue. There is no top-level `diagnostics` alias.
424	
425	Inputs accept `traversableGraph`, `syntheticRoot`, `rootWorkDependencies`, and `dependsOnWorkDefault`; async preparation also accepts `concurrency`. Preparation eagerly discovers and validates without visitors or execution events. Visitors, completed-work seeds, injected continuation state, and source replacements belong outside this input. Source errors retain exact identity, even when the caller throws a `DagTraversalStallError`; malformed source contracts also throw rather than becoming invalid results.
426	
427	Engine-originated structural discovery cycles return an invalid preparation issue `{ kind: 'discoveryCycle', cycleWitnessVertexIds: readonly ID[] }`. The IDs retain the engine's ordered closed witness (first ID repeated at the end) and arbitrary caller identity; for `a -> b -> a` the discovered closing edge yields `['b', 'a', 'b']`. This witness differs from the unordered SCC membership in authored-definition `structuralCycle` issues. Direct runner execution and runner `prepare()` still throw `DagDiscoveryCycleError<ID = unknown>`, exported from the root, core and DAG subpaths, with the same readonly frozen `cycleWitnessVertexIds` witness. Structural SCC issues use `componentVertexIds`. Source-thrown values, including instances of that class or `DagTraversalStallError`, propagate unchanged across callback, getter and iterable reads. Collection adapters reject missing child IDs eagerly with `TypeError`, before preparation starts. Dependency invalidity appears in the `milestone` issue within `invalid.issues`.
428	
429	`dag.liveVertexSummaries` is a convenience projection of live vertices, not a round-trip source; its `children` omits omission slots. Use `dag.definition` for faithful reconstruction, composition and revision. The projection is a detached readonly array of descriptions: `{ vertexId, data, children, dependsOnWork, dependsOnSubgraphCompletion }`. Owned records and edge arrays are immutable, while data and IDs retain shallow caller identity. The definition preserves structural order, single-root versus multiple-entry semantics, omissions satisfying prerequisites, effective implicit dependencies, and the original root W policy. Replay normalizes discovery hints to ID links; original opaque hints and callback contexts are not captured.
430	
431	| Factory                                | Result                                                         | Options                                                                       |
432	| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
433	| `dag.createRunner(options?)`           | Prepared sync `DagTraversalRunner`                             | `visitors`, `completedWork`, `workCompletion`, `retainOriginalGraphStructure` |
434	| `dag.createAsyncRunner(options?)`      | Promise of a prepared async runner                             | Same options, plus `concurrency`                                              |
435	| `dag.createWorkSession(options?)`      | `DagWorkSession<ID>` using external settlement                 | `completedWork`                                                               |
436	| `dag.createAsyncWorkSession(options?)` | Promise of `AsyncDagWorkSession<ID>` using external settlement | `completedWork`, `concurrency`                                                |
437	
438	Each factory creates independent references, progress, visitors, seed copies, and settlement generations. New runners prepare replay topology before visitors execute and never call original source adapters. Replay may repeat in-memory validation. Runner data/hint types are `VertexTypes<Data, ID>`; event/visitor phase selection remains available through ordinary runner execution methods. The definition owns topology: attempts to replace sources, discovery/root/implicit-parent policies, sorting, or continuation state reject, including JavaScript own fields explicitly set to `undefined`. Session factories accept only the options listed above; use a custom configured runner plus coordination when visitors are needed.
439	
440	A prepared definition is an in-memory value, not a durable checkpoint or editable graph. Reconstruct from source facts after process loss and create a new definition for a new graph revision. The [foundations example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/agent-api-foundations-example.ts) verifies independent sessions and no original-source replay.
441	
442	#### Materialized DAG definitions
443	
444	`dag.definition` is a `DagDefinition<Data, ID>` containing ordered `vertices` (`vertexId`, `data`, `slots`, `dependsOnWork`, `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion`), `omittedIds`, and an `entry` tagged as `root`, `roots`, or `empty`. Dependencies are the captured effective W/C constraints. A definition slot is `{ kind: 'vertex', vertexId }` or `{ kind: 'omitted', identity: { vertexId } | null }`; the wrapper preserves a known `undefined` identity separately from an anonymous omission. Resolved-graph `ChildSlot` uses the same explicit identity wrapper for this distinction. Anonymous omission slots in vertex records remain stored, while replay filters them without inventing ID hints. Root catalog slots require identities; repeated slots and shared children are allowed.
445	
446	`defineDag(input)` copies and freezes owned arrays and records, retaining shallow caller data and ID references. Malformed required fields and duplicate live/omitted identity declarations throw `TypeError`. SameValueZero identity applies throughout, including dependency deduplication. Shape normalization does not validate graph semantics.
447	
448	`prepareDagDefinition(definition)` normalizes and validates those source facts without callbacks or execution events. It returns `PrepareDagResult<Data, ID>`: `{ kind: 'valid', dag }` or `{ kind: 'invalid', issues }`. Invalid results have no executable DAG. Valid results retain authored declaration order, ordered slots, and entry mode, and support all prepared factories above. Programmer errors and exact accessor-thrown values propagate.
449	
450	| Issue kind                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                            |
451	| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
452	| `missingStructuralEndpoint` | A vertex slot targets a non-live ID; `parent: { vertexId }` identifies the owner, and `parent: null` denotes a roots entry slot.                                                                   |
453	| `invalidEntry`              | `reason` is `unknownRoot`, `anonymousCatalogEntry`, or `emptyWithVertices`; `vertexIds` names the offending root/live records, or is empty for an anonymous entry. Root entries require a live ID. |
454	| `invalidOmission`           | `vertexIds` lists identified omission slots absent from the declared omitted domain, including references to live IDs.                                                                             |
455	| `unreachable`               | `vertexIds` lists declared live or omitted identities outside the entry closure through structural slots and both W/C dependency lists. Detached prerequisites are valid.                          |
456	| `structuralCycle`           | `componentVertexIds` is structural SCC membership in declaration order, rather than an ordered cycle witness.                                                                                      |
457	| `milestone`                 | `diagnostics` contains the existing `DagTraversalStallDiagnostics<ID>` for unknown W/C endpoints or combined milestone cycles.                                                                     |
458	
459	Structural issues are deterministic and prevent replay; structurally valid definitions use the existing DAG milestone validator. Empty entries may retain known omitted IDs, including an omitted root, and those IDs remain recognized for completed-work seeds. An empty entry with live records is invalid. This API represents in-memory source topology; it carries no runner progress or automatic completion-fact migration.
460	
461	#### Validation results and failures
462	
463	Expected graph invalidity is a **result**, programmer/contract errors are **exceptions**, and execution failures can be **retained runner failures**. Source callbacks may throw or reject any value, including null/undefined; preserve it rather than assuming every failure is an Error. Message strings are explanatory text, not stable error codes.
464	
465	| Operation                                               | Expected result / boundary                                                                                        | Failure behavior and consumer action                                                                                                                                                  |
466	| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
467	| `prepareDag` / `prepareDagAsync`                        | valid DAG or invalid issues; engine discovery cycles use `discoveryCycle`, dependency invalidity uses `milestone` | Malformed contracts and exact caller failures throw/reject. Render expected issues by discriminant.                                                                                   |
468	| `prepareDagDefinition` / `composeDag` / `reviseDag`     | valid DAG or invalid definition/milestone issues                                                                  | Invalid programmer inputs, collisions or nonexistent wire endpoints throw TypeError; revision leaves original sessions unchanged.                                                     |
469	| `defineDagFragment`                                     | Fragment directly                                                                                                 | Closed-definition invalidity throws `DagFragmentValidationError.issues`; malformed shapes/ports throw ordinary TypeError.                                                             |
470	| Direct runner `prepare()` / `run()` / iteration         | Prepared, paused, awaiting settlement or finished lifecycle boundary as applicable                                | Engine cycles/stalls and caller failures throw; execution retains exact failure for subsequent attempts. Preparation/execution ownership misuse rejects without taking another owner. |
471	| `session.advance()`                                     | awaitingSettlement, paused, finished                                                                              | A failed runner throws its retained exact error; switch on boundary.kind before reading workTickets.                                                                                  |
472	| `completeWork(ticket)` / `failTraversal(ticket, error)` | accepted or alreadyAccepted receipt                                                                               | Foreign/copied/conflicting/stale tickets reject before settlement mutation. Fatal failure affects the whole traversal; retryable attempts remain host-deferred.                       |
473	| `runner.settle(id, outcome, generation)`                | true on acceptance, false on identical replay                                                                     | Invalid identity/generation/conflict throws; local generations are not durable attempt IDs.                                                                                           |
474	| Builder `configure(patch)` / execution options          | Validated update                                                                                                  | Unsupported or malformed keys throw TypeError atomically; prior configuration/owner remains.                                                                                          |
475	| `rewriteObject` / `getOutputResult()`                   | Tagged present/absent output                                                                                      | Final getter requires FINISHED. Caller conversion failures propagate exactly and do not cache a successful conversion.                                                                |
476	| `requireVertexId` / `requirePathsTo` / `requirePathTo`  | Required ID/path                                                                                                  | Absent handles throw; use has/nullable siblings for optional lookup. Valid null/undefined IDs are not failure sentinels.                                                              |
477	| Walking iterator return / runner close                  | Return pauses; successful close is terminal                                                                       | Pending host promises must settle. Failed close rethrows the retained failure and does not repeat cleanup.                                                                            |
478	
479	##### Narrow invalid issues
480	
481	This executable example distinguishes source discovery-cycle evidence from milestone diagnostics. Authored-definition structural SCCs have a separate `structuralCycle` discriminator and `componentVertexIds` field.
482	
483	<!-- standalone -->
484	
485	```ts
486	import {
487	  materializeDagInputFromRecords,
488	  prepareDag,
489	  type DagDefinitionIssue,
490	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
491	
492	function describe<ID>(issue: DagDefinitionIssue<ID>): string {
493	  switch (issue.kind) {
494	    case 'discoveryCycle':
495	      return `closed witness: ${issue.cycleWitnessVertexIds.length} IDs`;
496	    case 'structuralCycle':
497	      return `structural component: ${issue.componentVertexIds.length} IDs`;
498	    case 'milestone':
499	      return `unknown prerequisites: ${issue.diagnostics.unknownPrerequisiteIds.length}`;
500	    default:
501	      return issue.kind; // Other authored-definition issue kinds are listed above.
502	  }
503	}
504	const cycle = prepareDag(
505	  materializeDagInputFromRecords(
506	    [
507	      { id: 'a', children: ['b'] },
508	      { id: 'b', children: ['a'] },
509	    ],
510	    { id: (item) => item.id, children: (item) => item.children },
511	  ),
512	);
513	if (
514	  cycle.kind !== 'invalid' ||
515	  describe(cycle.issues[0]!) !== 'closed witness: 3 IDs'
516	) {
517	  throw new Error('Expected a structured discovery-cycle result');
518	}
519	const missing = prepareDag(
520	  materializeDagInputFromRecords(
521	    [{ id: 'task', requires: ['not-in-catalog'] }],
522	    { id: (item) => item.id, dependsOnWork: (item) => item.requires },
523	  ),
524	);
525	if (
526	  missing.kind !== 'invalid' ||
527	  describe(missing.issues[0]!) !== 'unknown prerequisites: 1'
528	) {
529	  throw new Error('Expected milestone diagnostics');
530	}
531	```
532	
533	Do not catch and convert all source errors into invalid. The preparing engine recognizes its own failures; a source-thrown instance of the same class is still the caller's exact failure. Source preparation performs no work callbacks, so report invalid inputs before dispatch.
534	
535	##### Duplicate completion and fatal failure
536	
537	A duplicate accepted report is harmless; fatal failure is a deliberate whole-run decision. This is separate from a retryable host attempt, which should leave its ticket unsettled.
538	
539	<!-- standalone -->
540	
541	```ts
542	import {
543	  materializeDagInputFromRecords,
544	  prepareDag,
545	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
546	
547	const result = prepareDag(
548	  materializeDagInputFromRecords([{ id: 'work' }], { id: (item) => item.id }),
549	);
550	if (result.kind !== 'valid') throw new Error('Expected a valid graph');
551	const session = result.dag.createWorkSession();
552	const boundary = session.advance();
553	if (boundary.kind !== 'awaitingSettlement') throw new Error('Expected work');
554	const ticket = boundary.workTickets[0]!;
555	// A real host durably accepts the result before reporting completion.
556	if (
557	  session.completeWork(ticket).kind !== 'accepted' ||
558	  session.completeWork(ticket).kind !== 'alreadyAccepted' ||
559	  session.advance().kind !== 'finished'
560	) {
561	  throw new Error('Expected idempotent completion');
562	}
563	const failed = result.dag.createWorkSession();
564	const waiting = failed.advance();
565	if (waiting.kind !== 'awaitingSettlement') throw new Error('Expected work');
566	const exactFailure = Symbol('host-declared fatal failure');
567	failed.failTraversal(waiting.workTickets[0]!, exactFailure);
568	let caught = false;
569	try {
570	  failed.advance();
571	} catch (error) {
572	  if (error !== exactFailure) throw error;
573	  caught = true;
574	}
575	if (!caught) throw new Error('Expected the retained exact failure');
576	```
577	
578	#### Definition diffs
579	
580	`diffDagDefinitions(before, after)` compares immutable `DagDefinition` values and returns a `DagDefinitionDiff<ID>` with frozen owned arrays and records. It performs no preparation, execution, serialization or deep traversal. The definitions may have different data types; IDs retain their caller identity.
581	
582	- `addedIds` follows new vertex order; `removedIds` follows old vertex order.
583	- `changedVertices` contains retained IDs in old vertex order, each with `aspects` in the fixed order `data`, `slots`, `workDependencies`, `subgraphCompletionDependencies`.
584	- `vertexOrderChanged` compares the full ordered live-ID sequence, so additions and removals also set it. Reordering alone does not add a changed vertex record.
585	- `entryChanged` compares entry mode and its ordered contents. `omissionsChanged` compares the ordered omitted-ID declarations.
586	
587	IDs use SameValueZero throughout, including slots and dependencies. Slot kind and omission identity wrappers remain significant: anonymous omission differs from known `undefined`. Slot, dependency and omission ordering changes count. Data uses `Object.is`: replacing a data object counts even if its fields are equal; same-reference deep mutation cannot be detected. The host decides whether artifacts and accepted completion facts remain valid; the diff does not infer business invalidation.
588	
589	### Validated DAG revisions
590	
591	`reviseDag<Data, ID>(prepared, operations)` returns `DagRevisionResult<Data, ID>`: `{ kind: 'valid', dag, changes }` or `{ kind: 'invalid', issues }`. Only a valid result exposes a fresh prepared DAG. The prepared value fixes the data/ID domain; operations cannot widen it. All revision functions and types are exported from the root, DAG subpath and `dagTraversal` namespace.
592	
593	`DagRevisionOperation<Data, ID>` is a readonly tagged union:
594	
595	| Kind                      | Required payload                          | Effect                                                                      |
596	| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
597	| `addVertex`               | `vertex: DagDefinitionVertex<Data, ID>`   | Append a full live declaration; an existing live ID throws `TypeError`.     |
598	| `replaceVertex`           | `vertex: DagDefinitionVertex<Data, ID>`   | Replace a full declaration in place; an unknown live ID throws `TypeError`. |
599	| `removeVertexDeclaration` | `vertexId: ID`                            | Remove only that declaration; an unknown live ID throws `TypeError`.        |
600	| `replaceEntry`            | `entry: DagDefinition<Data, ID>['entry']` | Replace the root/roots/empty entry.                                         |
601	| `replaceOmissions`        | `omittedIds: readonly ID[]`               | Replace the ordered known-omission declarations.                            |
602	
603	Operations apply in order to a private candidate. Removal does not prune references, delete descendants or satisfy work. A batch may leave intermediate dangling references and repair them before final validation through `prepareDagDefinition`. Expected graph invalidity returns the same [definition issues](#materialized-dag-definitions); malformed shapes, duplicate final identity declarations and programmer errors throw `TypeError`. Exact caller-thrown values propagate. Rejected and successful batches leave the original definition and sessions unchanged. Empty batches also return a fresh prepared value. Owned topology is copied/frozen; data and IDs remain shallow caller values.
604	
605	`changes` is the [definition diff](#definition-diffs) between the original and final definitions, including vertex order. The diff reports declarations, not artifact validity. Old tickets remain governed by their original session and throw in new sessions. Revision neither cancels nor transfers admitted async callbacks, generations, progress, accepted facts or host revision IDs. New sessions start without completed work unless the host explicitly supplies an independently accepted `completedWork` set. Session factories still own their visitors; for callback execution use `createAsyncRunner({ visitors, workCompletion: 'externalSettlement' })` with `bindAsyncDagWorkSession`.
606	
607	See the [revision example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-revision-example.ts) for an isolated old ticket and host-selected completion facts.
608	
609	### DAG fragments and composition
610	
611	`defineDagFragment(definition, ports)` creates a `DagFragment<Data, ID, Port>` from a closed valid definition and a record of string-named live vertex IDs. It copies/freezes owned topology and port wrappers; caller data and IDs stay shallow and unfrozen. Port names retain literal keys. A closed-definition validation failure throws `DagFragmentValidationError<ID = unknown> extends TypeError`, exported from the root and DAG subpath, with `issues: readonly DagDefinitionIssue<ID>[]`. The issue array is copied shallowly; issue records and caller IDs retain identity. Successful construction still returns the fragment directly. Malformed definitions, unknown or omitted ports, and symbol port names remain ordinary `TypeError`s. Local W/C endpoints must resolve within the live/omitted domain; add external edges during composition.
612	
613	`mapDagFragmentIds(fragment, { mapId })` returns a `DagFragment<Data, MappedID, Port>` with `{ definition, ports }`. It calls `mapId` once per declared live identity in vertex order, then once per omitted identity in declaration order, caching results across entry, slots, W/C lists, omissions and ports. Arbitrary identities, including objects, symbols, `undefined` and `NaN`, retain SameValueZero semantics. Mapped live/live, live/omitted and omitted/omitted collisions throw ordinary `TypeError`. Instantiation revalidates the definition before mapping and uses `DagFragmentValidationError` for that validation branch. Caller-thrown mapping/accessor values propagate unchanged. As with stall errors, `instanceof` alone does not recover the caller's ID type from an arbitrary catch. No ID scheme or name binding is implicit.
614	
615	`composeDag(instances, options?)` returns `PrepareDagResult<Data, ID>`. Entries concatenate in instance order beneath a hidden roots holder. Root entries contribute a vertex slot, roots entries retain ordered slots, and empty entries contribute ordered known omitted slots. An entirely empty instance contributes no slot. Vertex/omission declaration order, internal slots, and structurally detached prerequisite components are preserved.
616	
617	`DagCompositionOptions<ID>` has two independent ordered lists:
618	
619	- `children: { parent: ID, child: ID }[]` appends structural slots without adding parent-work dependencies.
620	- `dependencies: { dependent: ID, prerequisite: { vertexId: ID, milestone: 'work' | 'subgraphCompletion' } }[]` appends explicit W/C waits without adding structural links. SameValueZero duplicates normalize within each dependency list.
621	
622	Cross-instance identity collisions and nonexistent wire endpoints throw `TypeError`. Structural parents/children and dependency dependents must be live; W/C prerequisites may also name known omitted identities. Wire endpoint fields and prerequisite `vertexId`/`milestone` must be own properties; an explicitly owned `undefined` ID remains valid. Invalid milestone names throw `TypeError`. For connections between existing endpoints, structural or combined W/C cycles return `{ kind: 'invalid', issues }` through the same validator as `prepareDagDefinition`, with no executable DAG. Inputs remain unchanged. Composition creates topology without carrying progress, tickets or accepted completion facts into a new session.
623	
624	<!-- standalone -->
625	
626	```ts
627	import {
628	  defineDag,
629	  defineDagFragment,
630	  mapDagFragmentIds,
631	  composeDag,
632	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
633	
634	const local = defineDag<string, 'task'>({
635	  vertices: [
636	    {
637	      vertexId: 'task',
638	      data: 'build',
639	      slots: [],
640	      dependsOnWork: [],
641	      dependsOnSubgraphCompletion: [],
642	    },
643	  ],
644	  omittedIds: [],
645	  entry: { kind: 'root', vertexId: 'task' },
646	});
647	const fragment = defineDagFragment(local, { start: 'task' });
648	const first = mapDagFragmentIds(fragment, {
649	  mapId: (local) => ({ project: 'first', local }),
650	});
651	const second = mapDagFragmentIds(fragment, {
652	  mapId: (local) => ({ project: 'second', local }),
653	});
654	const result = composeDag([first, second], {
655	  dependencies: [
656	    {
657	      dependent: second.ports.start,
658	      prerequisite: {
659	        vertexId: first.ports.start,
660	        milestone: 'subgraphCompletion',
661	      },
662	    },
663	  ],
664	});
665	if (result.kind === 'valid') result.dag.createRunner().run();
666	```
667	
668	For heterogeneous fragments, declare the data and ID unions explicitly with `composeDag<DataA | DataB, IdA | IdB>(instances, options)`. Options cannot widen an inferred identity domain to admit foreign wire IDs. All functions and public types are exported from the root and DAG subpath. See the [runnable fragment example](https://github.com/dany-fedorov/configurable-tree-traversal/blob/main/examples/dag-fragments-example.ts) for independent ticket-based sync/async execution.
669	
670	### Ticket coordination
671	
672	`bindDagWorkSession(runner)` and `bindAsyncDagWorkSession(runner)` require runners configured with `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'`. Wrapping executes nothing and creates no additional execution owner. Callers retain direct runner access; existing single-owner rules apply.
673	
674	| Operation                                                   | Result and contract                                                                                                                                                                                       |
675	| ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
676	| `advance()`                                                 | Drains the runner, then returns `{ kind: 'awaitingSettlement', workTickets }`, `{ kind: 'paused' }`, or `{ kind: 'finished' }`. Async advance returns a promise; failures throw the exact original value. |
677	| `completeWork(ticket)`                                      | Reports accepted work completion; returns `{ kind: 'accepted' }` initially and `{ kind: 'alreadyAccepted' }` for identical replay.                                                                        |
678	| `failTraversal(ticket, error)`                              | Reports fatal traversal failure; same acceptance result union. Identical failure replay compares errors with `Object.is`; conflicting reports reject.                                                     |
679	| `summary()`                                                 | Returns the runner's detached `DagSummary<ID>` without execution or source I/O.                                                                                                                           |
680	| `getStatus()`, `getStopReason()`, `isHalted()`, `inspect()` | Shared `TraversalExecutionState` observations of the coordinated runner.                                                                                                                                  |
681	| `inspectMilestones()`                                       | Captures a detached `DagMilestoneSnapshot<ID>` for dependency explanations and queries without advancing execution.                                                                                       |
682	| `requestPause()`                                            | Returns the runner's boolean cooperative pause request result; admitted callbacks drain before pause acknowledgement.                                                                                     |
683	
684	Dispatch external work from `advance()`'s `awaitingSettlement.workTickets`, after host claim/capacity checks. `workCompleted` iterator events report committed W and cannot request dispatch; an enabled `ON_WORK_READY` visitor runs before work and can dispatch directly. Use `summary()` for progress, `inspectMilestones()` for dependency explanations, and `inspect()` for shared execution/iterator state.
685	
686	`DagWorkBoundary<ID>` discriminates the three advance results; its `workTickets` contains readonly `DagWorkTicket<ID>` objects exposing only `vertexId`. The type-only nominal ticket declaration has no runtime constructor; spreading a ticket loses its private TypeScript identity. Hidden provenance binds each ticket to its issuing facade and deferred generation. Foreign, copied, forged, and stale tickets reject before settlement mutation. Repeated observations of the same deferred work remain usable. Tickets do not transfer between two facades wrapping the same runner. The existing settlement implementation owns duplicate and conflict behavior.
687	
688	`failTraversal(ticket, error)` is the sole fatal settlement method. Sessions expose inspection directly, including `session.inspectMilestones().explain({ vertexId, milestone: 'work' })`; snapshots do not change after later settlements.
689	
690	Observation does not advance execution, but it is not constant-cost: `inspectMilestones()` captures the current dependency graph, and summaries on lazy DAGs diagnose topology in O(V + E) while it differs from successfully validated topology. Prepared/eager runners reuse successful topology validation.
691	
692	Tickets are local capabilities with no durable serialized representation. Persist host-accepted completion facts, then call `completeWork(ticket)` and advance to observe newly eligible work. Tickets provide neither external claims nor retry/attempt policy. Fatal failure applies to the whole traversal; keep retryable work deferred under host policy.
693	
694	`DagWorkSessionControl` exposes concrete `TreeDagExecutionInspection<DagVisitorPhase>` through `inspect()` on both session families. `bindDagWorkSession`/`bindAsyncDagWorkSession` wrap shared runner progress; prepared DAG session factories create independent progress. Stall dependency records use `{ vertexId, unmetPrerequisiteIds }`.
695	
696	### Filtered DAG visitors
697	
698	`filterDagDataVisitor(predicate, callback)` and `filterAsyncDagDataVisitor(predicate, callback)` wrap ordinary DAG visitors. The synchronous predicate sees vertex **data**. A type guard narrows the callback's first argument; a boolean predicate filters without narrowing. The callback receives `(data, context)`, retaining the ordinary graph, reference, phase, group metadata, and command-result types. A false predicate invokes no callback and returns no commands. The async helper supports value-or-promise callbacks; predicate and callback errors preserve exact identity.
699	
700	#### Filtered visitor example
701	
702	Both helpers narrow only the callback data, preserving the ordinary family context and commands. This standalone recipe runs independent sync/async visitors over the same prepared catalog; the async callback awaits its own work before returning.
703	
704	<!-- standalone -->
705	
706	```ts
707	import {
708	  materializeDagInputFromRecords,
709	  prepareDag,
710	  DagVisitorPhase,
711	  filterDagDataVisitor,
712	  filterAsyncDagDataVisitor,
713	} from 'configurable-tree-traversal';
714	
715	type Task = { kind: 'task'; id: string; prompt: string };
716	type Group = { kind: 'group'; id: string };
717	type Work = Task | Group;
718	const records: Work[] = [
719	  { kind: 'group', id: 'bundle' },
720	  { kind: 'task', id: 'implement', prompt: 'Implement the feature' },
721	];
722	const prepared = prepareDag(
723	  materializeDagInputFromRecords(records, {
724	    id: (item) => item.id,
725	  }),
726	);
727	if (prepared.kind !== 'valid') throw new Error('Expected a valid catalog');
728	const prompts: string[] = [];
729	prepared.dag
730	  .createRunner({
731	    visitors: {
732	      [DagVisitorPhase.ON_WORK_READY]: filterDagDataVisitor(
733	        (data: Work): data is Task => data.kind === 'task',
734	        (task) => {
735	          prompts.push(task.prompt);
736	        },
737	      ),
738	    },
739	  })
740	  .run();
741	const asyncPrompts: string[] = [];
742	const asyncRunner = await prepared.dag.createAsyncRunner({
743	  concurrency: 2,
744	  visitors: {
745	    [DagVisitorPhase.ON_WORK_READY]: filterAsyncDagDataVisitor(
746	      (data: Work): data is Task => data.kind === 'task',
747	      async (task) => {
748	        asyncPrompts.push(await Promise.resolve(task.prompt));
749	      },
750	    ),
751	  },
752	});
753	await asyncRunner.run();
754	if (
755	  prompts.join(',') !== 'Implement the feature' ||
756	  asyncPrompts.join(',') !== prompts.join(',')
757	) {
758	  throw new Error('Expected narrowed task callbacks only');
759	}
760	```
761	
762	The host defines `Task`, `Group`, and their discriminants. The helper preserves callback ordering, command handling, and phase restrictions, including exclusive `DEFER_WORK_COMPLETION` only in `ON_WORK_READY`. Filtering alone does not defer work under `afterWorkReadyChain`; use external settlement when the host owns completion.
763	
764	### Discovery and execution as separate phases
765	
766	A DAG can be used in a **discover first, execute later** mode. Hints describe
767	how to find vertices and their structural children; dependencies describe when
768	their work is eligible. These relationships need not have the same shape.
769	
770	| Concern                  | Declared through                                                                           | Meaning                                                                                  |
771	| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
772	| Discovery and structure  | `resolveRoot()`, `resolveChild(hint)`, and `$childHints` child hints                       | Find vertices and establish structural parent/child relationships.                       |
773	| Work prerequisites       | `dependsOnWork` vertex IDs                                                                 | Hold a vertex's initial work until its prerequisites have completed their work.          |
774	| Completion prerequisites | `dependsOnSubgraphCompletion` vertex IDs                                                   | Hold initial work until the prerequisite vertices and their retained subgraphs complete. |
775	| Work completion          | Normal initial visitor-chain completion, `completedWork`, or successful guarded `settle()` | Supply the completion facts that release dependents.                                     |
776	| Subtree completion       | Structural children and the `ON_SUBGRAPH_READY` lifecycle                                  | Wait for a vertex's own work and its discovered descendant subgraph to complete.         |
777	
778	For example, a synthetic root can list a flat catalog of `a`, `b`, `c`, and `d`.
779	Every real vertex can have `$childHints: []`, while `dependsOnWork` declares a diamond:
780	
781	| Vertex | Child hints (`$childHints`) | Prerequisites (`dependsOnWork`) |
782	| ------ | --------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
783	| `a`    | `[]`                        | `[]`                            |
784	| `b`    | `[]`                        | `['a']`                         |
785	| `c`    | `[]`                        | `['a']`                         |
786	| `d`    | `[]`                        | `['b', 'c']`                    |
787	
788	All four vertices are discoverable through the catalog. Initially only `a` is
789	ready; completing it releases `b` and `c`, and `d` waits for both. No child hint
790	from `a` to `b` or from `b` to `d` is needed to express these prerequisites.
791	Discovery order does not satisfy a dependency or override its readiness rule.
792	It can still influence FIFO order among equally ready vertices.
793	
794	Graph sources default to `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'none'`: omitting `dependsOnWork`
795	means no work prerequisites. Set `dependsOnWorkDefault: 'discoveryParentWork'` to inherit discovery-parent W
796	only for omitted lists. Explicit `dependsOnWork: []` or an ID list always wins. Children of
797	a synthetic catalog root have no implicit dependency on the catalog holder.
798	Real child hints still define structure, paths, and subtree-completion
799	obligations even when work dependencies are supplied separately.
800	
801	With `discovery: 'eager'`, the runner resolves all reachable hints and validates
802	the declared dependencies before invoking any visitor. Discovery adapters should
803	describe or fetch graph facts; put the work being scheduled in visitors or in
804	the host executor. Resolving a vertex does not itself complete its work. Internal
805	dependency bookkeeping and supplied completion seeds may be processed during
806	discovery. Default lazy mode interleaves discovery and execution instead. For a separate preview boundary, use `prepare()` as described below.
807	
808	Both DAG runners expose `prepare(): this` / `Promise<this>`. On fresh tree-source or graph-source runners without injected traversal state/containers, preparation fully discovers the closure exposed by roots, hints and prerequisite lookup and validates combined W/C constraints. It invokes no visitors, emits no execution events, commits no new real-vertex W/C and creates no deferred generations; `completedWork` seeds still supply accepted W. Empty/omitted-root previews succeed at `HALTED` / `prepared`, not FINISHED. Inspect `getResolvedGraphView()` and `summary()` before calling `run()` or iterating.
809	
810	Preparation adopts effective eager discovery even for lazy inputs, exposes that mode in summaries, and establishes eager topology freezing (hint rewrites/subtree disabling reject). Repeated preparation before execution is idempotent. Run adopts the discovered graph without repeating adapters. Preparation after execution starts, during another ownership operation, or with injected state/container objects (even empty ones) rejects recoverably. Failed preparation rethrows the exact stored error. Async preparation shares the existing owner/session: pause waits for already-admitted discovery callbacks without canceling them, then reports `paused`; another prepare continues or run adopts discovery and executes.
811	
812	For a host-controlled execution phase, combine eager discovery with a complete
813	synthetic-root catalog and `workCompletion: 'externalSettlement'`.
814	After `run()` reaches quiescence, read `summary().awaitingSettlement`; the host can execute
815	selected work and report accepted completion through guarded `settle()`, or
816	rebuild from `completedWork` on its next tick. Under the default `afterWorkReadyChain` policy, normal chain return completes W; under `externalSettlement`, even an empty or filtered chain defers. The
817	[deferred progress example below](#deferred-dag-progress-and-reconciliation)
818	implements this flat-catalog mode.
819	
820	Without `resolvePrerequisite`, a prerequisite ID does not itself discover or
821	fetch its vertex: every required vertex must be reachable through hints or
822	listed in the catalog. With that hook, the runner can request prerequisites
823	transitively before declaring them missing. Eager mode rejects unresolved
824	prerequisite IDs before visitors run. The adapter owns catalog completeness,
825	including disconnected components and cycles with no dependency-free source.
826	
827	### Discovery and completed work
828	
829	DAG graph sources accept `completedWork?: ReadonlySet<VertexId>` in both synchronous
